topics.title: Sparse routing and prefix memory
topics.explanation: Sparse routing and prefix-average memory were compared with capacity-matched and shared-core dense controls across text pools and seeds. Neither showed a stable general advantage. Tied and untied output heads define different controls, and prefix averaging is distinct from writable entity-state memory.

topics.title: Character, subword, and morphological pathways
topics.explanation: Character, n-gram and morphological pathways were compared with lookup and dense controls to test compositional representation. Their effects varied by task, with parameter count and tokenization contributing to the comparison. These pathways differ from an explicitly supervised character-equality matcher.

topics.title: Whole-word and token masking
topics.explanation: Paired whole-word and token-masking comparisons across two seeds found a task-dependent effect rather than universal superiority. Whole-word masking improved BLiMP, EWoK and Entity in both short-budget comparisons, while Supplement, COMPS and Reading did not show consistent gains.

topics.title: Backbone architecture and batch-size controls
topics.explanation: BERT and DeBERTa comparisons tested backbone choice together with model size and batch geometry; an additional batch-size control corrected part of the comparison. The results do not isolate individual positional-attention components. Complete scores correspond to the particular model and evaluation configurations tested.

topics.title: Recursive autoregressive training
topics.explanation: Recursive autoregressive training was reproduced on the permitted corpus and examined through tokenizer and Reading controls. Correcting the leading-space boundary narrowed but did not close the Reading discrepancy between public weights and local reproduction. The remaining difference cannot be attributed to corpus choice alone.

topics.title: Vocabulary, depth, width, and budget
topics.explanation: Vocabulary, depth and width change compression, embedding capacity and training cost together. Retraining with a budget-compliant tokenizer defines a different comparison from earlier studies using a larger-corpus tokenizer. Depth comparisons have completed endpoints; the earlier tokenizer results do not establish admissible small-data model performance.

topics.title: Frequency gating and fine-grained representations
topics.explanation: Support-gated compositional residual embeddings test whether fine-grained composition improves on ordinary lookup embeddings. The zero-gate model matched the reference, but the trained nonzero-gate endpoint did not improve it. The ordinary embedding term remains present at the large-gate limit; other gates and seeds remain untested candidates.

topics.title: Components of a mature training recipe
topics.explanation: Mature-recipe comparisons examined depth, width, vocabulary, LAMB optimization, sequence length and masking schedules. Component-specific contrasts and completed two-stage recipes answer different questions: a favorable bundled recipe does not identify the contribution of every component changed within it.

topics.title: Gated feed-forward and layer-weighting candidates
topics.explanation: GEGLU feed-forward layers, attention gates and layer weighting are proposed changes to the model's computation. No completed training comparison establishes their benefit in this research; their efficacy under the small-data budget remains untested.

topics.title: Aligned reformulation and correspondence
topics.explanation: Aligned simplification and reformulation were compared with wrong correspondence, source matching, exact repetition and separated presentation. WikiAuto, SynCSE and clean generated reformulations define different data comparisons. Their effects depend on task and control condition, and correcting AoA units changes the interpretation of earlier aggregate scores.

topics.title: Compact views and budget reinvestment
topics.explanation: Compact-view reinvestment shortens a second expression of each source and spends the saved budget on additional passage pairs. Pair count rises from 10,094 to 12,155 within a 423,520-word replacement block: about 20.4% more passage pairs in that block, not more documents across the entire collection. Compression, additional coverage and candidate admission are distinct parts of the construction.

topics.title: Adjacency, repetition, and presentation layout
topics.explanation: Compact views, exact repetition and broken adjacency test the contribution of local pairing, while block and interleaved breadth layouts test presentation. These interventions have different task and item effects and share a historical tokenizer boundary. Their contrast is not interchangeable with the later target-deletion experiment.

topics.title: Extractive compression and bridging text
topics.explanation: Balanced and wider extraction, together with source-attested fluent bridges, test whether coverage can be increased while preserving lexical and semantic fidelity. Prototype checks establish construction properties, not successful large-scale training with fluent bridges; lexical closure alone does not establish faithful meaning.

topics.title: Rule-based rewriting
topics.explanation: A completed deterministic rule-rewrite screen compared correct pairing, same-entity wrong pairing, source-only and shuffled controls. The four conditions produced task trade-offs rather than a joint improvement in the intended abilities. Token-aware row matching did not equalize every condition's visible-token exposure.

topics.title: Entity-mention consistency
topics.explanation: Entity-mention consistency was tested against both wrong-pair training and ordinary whole-word masking. A second seed and corrected decoy analysis weakened the broad-benefit interpretation. An advantage over destructive mismatches does not by itself establish useful consistency learning beyond ordinary prediction.

topics.title: Counterfactual and cross-span supervision
topics.explanation: Counterfactual propagation and cross-span supervision test newly acquired source dependencies separately from sensitivity already present in the model. Dependent, nondependent, local, wrong-source and absent-source controls distinguish these possibilities. Short training did not establish general relation acquisition.

topics.title: State text and directed masking
topics.explanation: State-coherent stories, relation-directed whole-word masking and evidence-visible or inverse-priority masking sometimes improved targeted behavior while imposing broader language costs. Near-identical early checkpoint tables have unresolved identity limitations and do not establish independently verified developmental trajectories.

topics.title: Auxiliary causal objectives
topics.explanation: Whole-batch causal replacement and gradient-calibrated shifted-token auxiliaries are distinct ways of combining causal and masked prediction. Completed full-model evaluation did not establish improvement over the corresponding reference. Near-aligned local gradients were therefore insufficient evidence of a useful combined objective.

topics.title: Self-sampled replaced-token detection
topics.explanation: Self-sampled replaced-token detection with detached sampling and embedding-gradient decoupling completed a 20M-word screen with task-dependent benefits and costs. Majority-class shortcuts and balanced detector performance are distinct tests of the auxiliary task. A delayed mature-model detection objective remains a proposal without a completed efficacy result.

topics.title: Target weighting and supervision coverage
topics.explanation: Word-mean losses, support floors, source-absent target weighting and directed cross-view masking test how prediction credit is allocated. Better fit on the selected targets can coexist with lower broad scores. Exact-swap target matching passed construction and short implementation checks but lacks a trained efficacy result.

topics.title: Relational pivots and counterfactual cues
topics.explanation: Pivot targets, sparsely calibrated auxiliary losses and spatial witnesses test whether supervision selects a relation or merely retrieves a visible answer. Matched supervision mass and erased or permuted controls distinguish those mechanisms. Low candidate yield and saturated retrieval performance limit claims of learned state selection.

topics.title: Gradient exchange and projection
topics.explanation: Centered four-condition exchange gradients and projected or row-centered alignment measure local relationships between learning signals. Same-row alternative negatives and gradient-norm calibration define the comparison. Orthogonality or a fitted alignment coefficient does not establish long-term learning benefit or retention.

topics.title: Coherent-context margin loss
topics.explanation: The coherent-context margin pilot did not produce the intended likelihood separation between coherent and broken contexts. Its endpoint decline cannot be attributed to the margin term alone because a matched zero-coefficient continuation was not evaluated.

topics.title: Adaptive masking granularity
topics.explanation: Adaptive masking and late switches from whole-word to token masking have stage-dependent effects that can reverse during training. Paired data-by-mask comparisons and complete trajectories show why an intermediate advantage need not survive the final budget, particularly when sequence and batch geometry differ.

topics.title: Data order and developmental curricula
topics.explanation: Same-content ordering, cadence and first-pass developmental curricula test different aspects of training experience. Prefix-truncation repairs also change the material actually seen, so a bundled recipe cannot isolate an ordering advantage. Occurrence-timing studies provide a separate, shorter-budget test of age-of-acquisition behavior.

topics.title: Context-length caps
topics.report_guide: The experiments and analyses for this topic are listed below. Related measurement principles are discussed in report section `sec:measurement_branch`.
topics.explanation: Context-cap comparisons hold pair dose fixed while changing training geometry. A large historical Overall difference was largely driven by the reference's negative AoA contribution, whereas the seven-family mean did not improve. The result is not a broad, simultaneous gain across language tasks.

topics.title: Optimizers and mature model states
topics.explanation: AdamW, LAMB and Muon comparisons, trust-ratio probes and mature-model switches depend on horizon and optimizer state. One LAMB configuration also changed other model settings and is not a single-optimizer ablation. An incomplete low-learning-rate condition does not provide an exposure-matched 20M-word comparison.

topics.title: Checkpoint averaging and restarts
topics.explanation: Stochastic weight averaging, adjacent-checkpoint averaging, tail restarts and another training seed distinguish checkpoint selection from a reproducible stabilization effect. Evaluated averages did not reliably exceed the selected checkpoint, and different sample panels could favor different exposure points.

topics.title: Relation dose and learning maturity
topics.explanation: Binding-dose and role-switch studies compare mature and weak bases, concentrated and sparse mixtures, and natural continuation. A learnable synthetic task does not establish acquisition from admissible natural-text pretraining. Additional diagnostic exposure and the nonneutral role-fixed comparator limit attribution to relation dose alone.

topics.title: Continued relation-training candidates
topics.explanation: RDGA local/full-context objectives and RMEC remention masking propose continued training on relation-dependent prediction. Their hypotheses and planned controls have no completed training comparison here; formulas, expected scores and implementation plans are not empirical results.

topics.title: Zero-initialized bottleneck branch
topics.explanation: A zero-output bottleneck residual preserves the initial model function and permits disabled-path controls, including bounded training-parity checks. Joint training still updates the base parameters. Initialization or short-horizon parity therefore does not imply a frozen-base trajectory throughout training.

topics.title: Main and auxiliary path separation
topics.explanation: Joint residual training, dual-view auxiliaries and main-disabled/auxiliary-enabled paths assign gradients to different parameters. Path-specific checks and item gains and losses showed that early recovery of difficult examples did not guarantee broad improvement or transfer to a mature model.

topics.title: Dedicated increments on a frozen base
topics.explanation: Frozen-parent continuation learns a dedicated increment using ordinary prediction and KL while the parent weights remain fixed. Coherent and span-broken replay form the closest matched pair; ordinary and shuffled alternatives differ in additional respects. Disabling the increment restores the parent structurally, but retention with it enabled is an empirical outcome.

topics.title: Model lineage and scale selection
topics.explanation: Stock compact models, continuous packing, jointly trained residuals and frozen-parent increments form separate branches rather than an additive ablation sequence. Repaired adapter-aware full evaluation defines the released-model comparison; older scores describe historical measurement conditions. Selecting an inference scale after evaluation changes the function but does not create another training replicate.

topics.title: Writing and reading with supplied addresses
topics.explanation: Supplied-address writable memory was tested with overwrites, distractors, slot interventions and eventwise address corruption. Consistent address renaming preserves the addressing relation and is a symmetry control. These functional results are distinct from the withdrawn query-independent tiny-memory task and do not establish learned routing from raw text.

topics.title: Answer shortcuts in a tiny binding task
topics.explanation: The early tiny-memory binding interpretation is withdrawn: answers followed action outcomes regardless of the queried entity. High accuracy and sensitivity to write permutation therefore do not establish query-conditioned binding. A corrected corpus and training script were constructed, but no completed successful corrected-model experiment is established.

topics.title: Routing from natural text to addresses
topics.explanation: Raw, lexical, recurrent and discrete routers test whether text can supply the addresses used by a state-memory mechanism. In one router, 90.4% token accuracy concealed zero query recall; predicted routing failed where supplied routing retained functional effects. This interface failure differs from the withdrawn answer-generator shortcut.

topics.title: Pointer and copy initialization
topics.explanation: Pointer and embedding-factorization initialization activated a copy pathway, but the repaired candidate-token readout still failed to select a property according to the queried entity. Active copying is therefore distinct from learned entity-property binding. This failure is separate from the query-independent answer shortcut in the withdrawn tiny-memory task.

topics.title: Format preadaptation and label alignment
topics.explanation: Format acquisition and inference-time tolerance test different aspects of reading. Aligned, permuted and disjoint-label preparation all helped a later task, weakening the claim that a particular learned address correspondence was essential. The comparison does not establish a universal head-only explanation.

topics.title: Frozen readers and within-group selection
topics.explanation: A frozen reader with a four-candidate group-softmax selector approached supplied-address performance on exact names and role swaps. Selecting prior versus revised states remained weaker, and stable examples inflated pooled accuracy. Explicit tags, candidate sets and direct supervision are conditions of the result.

topics.title: Identifiability of relational rules
topics.explanation: Initial-owner changes, alias balance and independent event or ranking reversals expose anti-copy shortcuts compatible with high training accuracy. These controls test whether the intended state-transition rule is identifiable. Success on a separate relation graph does not resolve ambiguity in the earlier task.

topics.title: Binary relation graphs and sparse anchors
topics.explanation: Binary relation graphs with sparse orientation anchors support sign propagation through shared representations. A three-seed core result is complemented by shared, untied and fully tied comparisons, anchor reversal and relation-closure tests. Supplied candidates, incomplete control fits and changed example counts after edge removal bound stronger necessity claims.

topics.title: Character identity and access to relational structure
topics.explanation: Finite full-alphabet equality supervision repairs identity matching and connects new character combinations to a shared relation graph. The construction uses a frozen matcher, hard assignment, supplied candidates and alphabet coverage. It does not establish unsupervised name understanding, alias resolution or unrestricted natural-language reference.

topics.title: Leakage-free graph and program construction
topics.explanation: Neutral and reversed graph packets and program-structured tasks test controlled relational data construction. Low clean yield, residual answer priors and leakage or type checks limit the prototypes. Scorer comparisons without verified model loading do not establish a confirmed functional mechanism.

topics.title: Structural density and representation recovery
topics.explanation: Structure-density and residualized selection scores mix source, compression and surface properties. Improved structure-readout fit did not establish broad learning gains. A separate corrected target-position binding screen tests a different task from the withdrawn tiny-memory study.

topics.title: Tail training on shared-source clusters
topics.explanation: Shared-anchor clustered tails outperformed some mismatches but not every repetition or untouched-tail control. Seen-versus-held sentence labels do not establish separation from pretraining exposure. Some complete endpoints remain unavailable, limiting claims beyond the measured comparisons.

topics.title: Views, breadth, and repetition under a fixed budget
topics.explanation: Fixed-budget view, breadth, repetition and clean-data substitutions estimate treatment effects specific to model architecture and learning stage. Late-window comparisons use different token budgets and task populations across architectures. Increased sentence coverage is not necessarily increased independent-document coverage, and incompatible populations do not define one pooled effect.

topics.title: Register substitution and data-value prediction
topics.explanation: Register substitution holds admitted content fixed while varying the displaced material, making opportunity cost part of data value. Word-level and profile-level Jensen-Shannon divergence predictors have different corrected definitions; mismatched windows or task sets do not yield a valid prediction error. Second-seed and in-corpus measurements extend the comparison without establishing a universal predictor.

topics.title: Selecting explicit relational text
topics.explanation: Relation-explicit FineWeb selection and natural state or spatial filters test whether usable relational examples can be identified from text. Their quality checks and short screens found limited clean yield, not a validated large-scale relation-training stream. Low yield under these filters does not imply that relations are intrinsically absent from natural text.

topics.title: Deletion of source-absent and copied targets
topics.explanation: Deleting source-absent versus copied targets holds input fixed with nearly matched supervision. Local source-pair-disjoint effects are positive, but stricter document-disjoint intervals cross zero, and target-loss and seven-task rankings differ. These comparisons do not identify mediation fractions or share an estimand with the earlier compact-view triangle.

topics.title: Correct, wrong, and missing sources
topics.explanation: True, wrong and missing-source interventions hold target tokens fixed to measure source-conditioned prediction. Large reformulation advantages also occur without direct supervision of the source-absent target channel. This separates the readout from that training channel but does not establish input-only learning or a causal explanation of final Overall.

topics.title: Coverage, order, and local context
topics.explanation: Source presence, prefix placement, gaps, order and window position change different aspects of available context. Text-only coverage counts can be established independently of model loading. Historical likelihood contrasts with unresolved loader identity do not provide verified evidence of a model mechanism.

topics.title: Ordered composition and dynamic binding
topics.explanation: Ordered dynamic and static tasks distinguish decoding local intermediate states from composing a final answer. Intermediate information could be accessible while final composition failed. Poorly fitted from-scratch controls and failed readouts do not establish architectural impossibility; training fit, candidate priors and held-symbol behavior constrain that inference.

topics.title: Contextual hidden states and interventions
topics.explanation: Same-entity history replacement and factorial activation interventions distinguish representational change from functional state use. Topic or entity information can affect hidden states without producing the correct state-dependent answer. Null interventions delimit particular pathways rather than every possible contextual computation.

topics.title: State updates in microworlds
topics.explanation: Micro-worlds separate explicit state statements, action inference, contradictory evidence and target-word-free overwriting. They provide controlled diagnostics but did not become validated selectors of natural-benchmark performance. These tests are distinct from the withdrawn tiny-memory claim of successful compositional binding.

topics.title: Gradient conflict and learning-signal estimation
topics.explanation: Gradient conflict, transfer gain per word and within-experience credit estimators were tested with blocked permutations, same-bag and cross-pair controls, and held objects. Local associations did not become stable prospective predictors of the value of additional learning experience.

topics.title: Contrastive prediction and auxiliary readouts
topics.explanation: Contrastive predictive coding and strict continuation objectives were examined with same-source, cross-source and difficult-negative readouts. Auxiliary fit or high retrieval accuracy could improve without establishing newly acquired identity-specific context use. Successful discrimination of an auxiliary task is not equivalent to learning the intended dependence.

topics.title: Layer-wise readouts and position editing
topics.explanation: Layer mixing, diagonal-bilinear and ridge readouts, and local position edits test accessible information and transfer. Training fit coexisted with held-condition failures, while rotated-null controls constrained the interpretation. A small morphology-heavy edit set does not establish a general circuit-level intervention result.

topics.title: Score changes under pair swaps
topics.explanation: Antisymmetric paired scores and cross-corpus contrasts test correspondence using category, length, target-swap and wrong-pair controls. Algebraic cancellation in a score and discrimination among existing models do not establish functional use of the relation or reliable selection of a better candidate model.

topics.title: Shared-parameter initialization
topics.explanation: Removing positional components changed random-number consumption, so the same seed did not give common tensors identical initial values. Copying all 140 shared tensors sharply reduced the apparent architecture-by-data interaction. This correction concerns relative treatment effects, not the claim that positional machinery is irrelevant to absolute ability.

topics.title: Macro averages and item-level changes
topics.explanation: Macro averages, gained and lost items, and oracle complementarity use different denominators and can disagree in sign. Item transitions and corrected percentage units explain why a higher task mean need not mean more examples answered correctly. A label-assisted oracle union is not a learned selector.

topics.title: Transfer conditions and representation geometry
topics.explanation: Cross-architecture transfer contrasts, baseline-conditioned slopes, seed differences and centered principal-component analyses did not establish a capability-conservation law. Shared-item matching defines the comparison, while unavailable loadings and limited seed variation constrain interpretation. An observed difference between two seeds is not a population noise estimate.

topics.title: Complete evaluation and model interfaces
topics.report_guide: Report appendix: `app:evaluation`. The experiments and analyses below provide the detailed measurement records.
topics.explanation: Complete evaluation depends on the full loaded model, task populations, AoA checkpoint trajectories and Reading or GlobalPIQA scoring semantics. Encoder-loader repairs can change the function evaluated. Missing measurements, measured zero, historical public displays and repaired local scores therefore represent distinct evidence conditions.

topics.title: Word boundaries, packing, and visible budgets
topics.explanation: Word-boundary packing, intact paired views, truncation and continuous-window visibility relate counted words to the tokens and targets actually seen. The U256 packing experiment is a separate branch, not an assumed ancestor of the final model. Corpus origin and the teacher used to generate reformulations are part of the definition of the training experience.

topics.title: Microbatches and gradient equivalence
topics.explanation: Target-count-weighted microbatch loss corrects the unequal weighting produced by averaging means over different numbers of targets. Deterministic reduction tests, activation-checkpoint guards, evaluator-batching checks and short trajectory comparisons establish bounded implementation properties, not identical stochastic training or a measured full-training speedup.

topics.title: Model reconstruction and cost breakdown
topics.explanation: Custom-model reconstruction depends on matching weights, configuration, model code and branch controls. Same-seed tensor reconstruction differs from new-seed replication and exact training resume. Parameter count, word exposure, updates, trainer time and total search or evaluation cost measure different resources; unavailable costs are not zero.

topics.title: Selectivity in relation learning
topics.research_family: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
topics.explanation: Across three training seeds, exact recurrence and aligned reformulation produced opposite changes in true-source advantage on compact targets without source-token overlap. A neutral ordinary-text context anchors the comparison. The result identifies relation-selective learning in this setting, not a universal harm from repetition.

topics.title: Prediction windows with matched materials
topics.research_family: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
topics.explanation: Row-split controls retain each recurrence or reformulation condition's material while moving source and companion outside the same prediction window. Two-seed neutral-anchor measurements show attenuation of the large source effects. Content matching holds within each local-versus-split pair, not between the recurrence and reformulation corpora.

topics.title: Transfer conditions for natural reformulations
topics.research_family: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
topics.explanation: Natural remention, Wikipedia/Simple-English and source-recurring versus source-absent targets reveal transfer that depends on relation and register. Wrong correspondence, exact copy and half-view dose controls delimit the effects. Separated-coexistence and exact row-split conditions differ in packing and are not interchangeable locality controls.

topics.title: Familiar performance and functional access with unseen symbols
topics.research_family: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
topics.explanation: Query-first binding tasks compare answer-focused preparation, ordinary full continuation, static credit and interleaving. Familiar-symbol performance can recover without recovery on held query symbols. Donor/recipient interventions and fitted-direction tests constrain the explanation within the controlled task, without establishing general natural-language transfer.

topics.title: Erasing and relocating functional signals
topics.research_family: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
topics.explanation: Centering, zeroing, rotation and donor replacement of an attribute-position component demonstrate its functional involvement in a controlled binding task. Refitted directions did not restore held-symbol transfer. The result neither excludes every distributed recoding nor establishes that all downstream computation remained intact.

topics.title: Dense inputs and sparse supervision
topics.research_family: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
topics.explanation: Sparse-input/sparse-target, dense-input/sparse-target and dense-input/dense-target conditions separate input corruption from focused supervision on existing text. Both complete dense-input/sparse-target continuations exceed matched ordinary continuation at equal exposure. Ordinary continuation also differs in target policy, and the sparse-input/sparse-target control lacks a complete nine-task endpoint.

topics.title: Preservation inputs and effective strength
topics.research_family: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
topics.explanation: Ordinary-state and dense-state preservation differ in input, target support and effective gradient strength. The KL is teacher-to-student; deterministic and random-state controls separate drift from stochastic disagreement. The common-position dense-to-ordinary gradient ratio is 11.835, so equal coefficients do not match strength. Attenuation and rollback explain part of the recovery.

topics.title: Principle-guided complete model
topics.research_family: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
topics.explanation: The complete policy and ordinary, dense-input/sparse-target and dense-input/dense-target controls share one pretrained parent and two continuation seeds. Repaired nine-task evaluations support the measured policy comparison, distinct from historical public displays. Full preservation adds 517,332 words, and most Overall gain comes from the small fixed GlobalPIQA set rather than uniform task improvement.

scope: Scientific reading map; one file may support several topics.
